frequency_question: What proportion of substantive renewals or replacements for expiring transboundary water treaties successfully complete formal signature and official confirmation within the designated final calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes any bilateral or multilateral river/water-sharing treaty expiring within a defined multi-year window where successor negotiations were active, requiring a formal signed text and official government release to count as a hit.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty continuous renewals and extensions
Columbia River Treaty modernization negotiations interim agreements
1995 Mekong Agreement successor to 1957 Mekong Committee statutes
Israeli-Jordanian Water Annex implementation and renewals
Lesotho Highlands Water Project phase updates

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 6 named major precedents; believed roughly 7 total globally for major federal-level river treaty renewals of this scale in the modern era.
known_gaps: Excludes minor municipal or sub-national water accords.
skeleton: Named historical precedents of major transboundary water treaty renewals and successor instruments over the last 65 years.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 major comparable historical renewal processes equals approximately 85 percent.
validity_reason: Base rate reflects long-term state practice regarding treaty renewals, stable across decades.
